g.text: One LuCI navigation: who does the work
Full page load vs same-document router
Cudy TR3000 · mediatek/filogic · ARMv8 · OpenWrt SNAPSHOT r0-20d94d5 · plain HTTP · warm cache · 2026-08-18
The two paths are directly comparable
Byte-identical to what it threw away
This is the only step that
TTFB 118 · HTML end 123 · i18n 124→209 · DOMContentLoaded 215 · first ubus 227 · last ubus 304
ubus window 2→56 · shell remains live · menus update state only
Two CGI dispatches re-derive a shell the browser already had, and a catalog it already held.
The router deletes exactly that. The view's data calls survive untouched — they simply start 225 ms earlier.
first ubus: 227 ms -> 2 ms · view painted: 321 ms -> 91 ms
02 · WHAT MOVED, AND WHAT DID NOT
Two whole CGI dispatches. Neither depended
on which page was asked for.
fork CGI + ucode VM x2 ................. 4 ms
menu tree stat + parse x2 .............. 24 ms
Two dispatches, 209 ms, on the slowest and most shared CPU in the system.
The cost is the dispatch, not the payload.
The empty English catalog is only 13 bytes and still costs 62.7 ms.
The router did not stop working — it stopped
the view's own ubus data calls
once per SESSION, not per navigation 68.2 ms
already cached; cheap to serve ....... 0.8 ms
one extra batched ubus call .......... kept
The view-specific RPC work remains on the router.
Only the repeated shell derivation disappears.
Dispatcher rules ported verbatim, plus the cleanup
document death used to do for free.
ACL fold down the dispatch path
page-scoped patch CSS/JS and node css state
state only — menus are not rebuilt
Getting this wrong shows up as stale state, not as a slow page.
That is why the resolver is a port of
Explicit teardown + one batched ubus refill.
Failure mode: stale state, not latency.
dispatch anatomy: fork + VM 2.2 · import 37.2 · menu tree 13.8 · session probe 6.0 ms
A 13-byte CGI response costs 62.7 ms; a 191,899-byte static file costs 0.8 ms.
n=10 each · same pages · warm cache
Range 50–87% · independent harness median 72% · full-load spread ±40 ms
Measured 2026-08-18. Source behavior verified against openwrt/luci master: ucode/dispatcher.uc · ucode/template/view.ut · ucode/template/header.ut · ucode/http.uc · ucode/controller/admin/index.uc
The ratio is the claim; the digits are not.
Numbers connect the timeline bars to the work below.
luci.dispatcher resolves menu, session and ACLs;
view.ut -> header.ut renders the document shell.
No destination-specific data has loaded yet.
A second CGI process runs admin/translations/<lang>.
The catalog is parser-blocking and uncacheable:
no-cache, no ETag and no Last-Modified.
The dispatch cost dominates the payload size.
The browser discards DOM, JS heap, timers and listeners;
then parses HTML, initializes LuCI and rebuilds navigation.
The shell is byte-identical to the previous one.
This is the only destination-specific step.
The view module and its data contract stay unchanged.
The view's existing load() ubus calls stay on the device.
Same work, same cost; they start 225 ms earlier.
Teardown also performs one batched uci refill.
Flush Poll, uci, listeners and modals; apply dispatcher rules;
update L.env, page state, menus, breadcrumbs and tabs.
